title: Kestrel and the Vector
premise: Petra Fairweather, an insurance investigator who has spent a decade hiding among cargo haulers in contested orbits, is assigned to the Kestrel, a deep-space survey ship that returned with its crew biologically aged backward. He discovers the reversal was no accident: the crew found an alien vector that rewrites time's direction, and both fleets want it as a weapon. To keep the truth buried, Petra fabricates a cover story that holds an uneasy peace between two armadas—but the lie demands constant feeding, and the reversed crew, led by engineer Sefa Ilo, are living proof with shrinking memories. When the fleets converge to seize the Kestrel, Petra must choose between exposing the vector and preserving the fragile peace, ending with him broadcasting the truth and surrendering himself, while Sefa—now younger than her own memories—carries their shared future forward.
about_author: Elodie Crane is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who traded harbor offices for orbital mechanics textbooks and never looked back. She writes science fiction about people whose jobs are too strange for job titles, from a converted lighthouse on the Atlantic coast.

chapters.title: Actuarial Odds
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Investigating a docking accident in contested orbit, he calculates blame with cold precision while dodging both fleets' customs drones. Establishes his invisibility as survival strategy. Emotional beat: competent loneliness—he's good at a job designed to be forgotten.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Home Young
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The Kestrel docks after eleven years; the crew is twenty years younger than their service records. Petra is assigned because no one else wants the impossible claim. Beat: professional curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Sefa Ilo Remembers Forward
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Kestrel's chief engineer recalls events that haven't happened yet, memories arriving like weather. She recognizes Petra's name from a future she can't explain. Beat: disorientation and eerie tenderness.

chapters.title: Paperwork for Miracles
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He interviews the crew, finding identical stories: a signal, a light, then waking younger. His report must be plausible enough to file and vague enough to hide. Beat: the first compromise of his integrity.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Question
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Both the Concord fleet and the Meridian Armada demand access to the Kestrel. Petra realizes his insurance ruling will decide which side boards first. Beat: the weight of being suddenly visible.

chapters.title: The Vector Hypothesis
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. In the engine room she shows Petra the residual field patterns—the ship didn't age backward by chance; something out there reached in and turned them around. Beat: wonder shadowed by terror.

chapters.title: A Lie With Good Posture
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He files a ruling calling it sensor corruption and radiation exposure—a tidy, boring explanation. Both fleets accept it provisionally. Beat: relief that feels like swallowing glass.

chapters.title: Ten Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, flashback-heavy. How he vanished into cargo work after testifying against a Concord admiral and losing everything. Beat: understanding why he lies so well—and what it cost him.

chapters.title: Coffee With Someone Who Knows
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. She and Petra share a meal; she describes his future kindnesses before he performs them. First real intimacy either has allowed in years. Beat: belonging, frightening and warm.

chapters.title: Meridian Auditors
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A Meridian investigator, Halvorsen, arrives unconvinced, poking holes in the radiation story. Petra must improvise faster than he can document. Beat: the lie begins demanding maintenance.

chapters.title: The Crew That Is Unbecoming
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The youngest-again crew members are losing adult memories entirely—one forgets her own children. The reversal isn't stable; it's still running. Beat: grief with a countdown attached.

chapters.title: Concord Summons
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The Concord fleet orders him to hand over the Kestrel's black box. Refusing means exposure; complying arms a weapon race. Beat: duty versus conscience, the old wound reopened.

chapters.title: What the Box Contains
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. She decrypts fragments of the black box: coordinates, a repeating mathematical invitation. The vector wasn't an attack—it was contact. Beat: awe reframing everything.

chapters.title: Halvorsen's Bargain
chapters.summary: Halvorsen's POV. The Meridian investigator privately offers Petra protection in exchange for the coordinates. He's not a villain—just a man who believes order prevents war. Beat: sympathy for the antagonist's logic.

chapters.title: A Future Worth Lying For
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Her forward-memories now include Petra standing in a broadcast room, choosing something terrible. She tells him nothing yet. Beat: love entangled with foreknowledge, guilt of omission.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Hold
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Someone tampers with the Kestrel's reactor to force an evacuation and legal seizure. Petra catches it barely, realizing both fleets have agents aboard. Beat: paranoia tightening the screws.

chapters.title: The Children of the Crew
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The most-reversed crew member, Ensign Okoro, now mentally a child, asks Sefa if she's her mother. Sefa lies gently. Beat: the human cost of the secret made unbearable.

chapters.title: Filing the Second Lie
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He fabricates reactor telemetry to explain the sabotage, deepening the cover story. Each lie now requires two more. Beat: the architecture of deception becoming a prison.

chapters.title: Concord Moves First
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A Concord strike team seizes the station's traffic control, preparing to board the Kestrel within days. Petra's ruling is now the only thing delaying war. Beat: the clock becomes audible.

chapters.title: Memories Like Incoming Tide
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Her future-memories flood: fleets burning, a station breaking apart, Petra's voice on open channels. She finally tells him what she's seen. Beat: confession as intimacy and burden at once.

chapters.title: The Middle of the Book Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Petra and Sefa spend one quiet night in the observation ring while both fleets maneuver outside. They admit they love each other without promising anything. Beat: stillness before the storm, earned tenderness.

chapters.title: Halvorsen Closes In
chapters.summary: Halvorsen's POV. He cross-references Petra's old testimony against the admiral and realizes why he lies so well. Confrontation: expose yourself or give me the coordinates. Beat: the past arriving to collect.

chapters.title: Okoro Runs
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Child-minded Okoro wanders into Meridian territory seeking 'the light that made her small.' Retrieving her nearly triggers gunfire. Beat: the secret fraying at its weakest thread.

chapters.title: The Ruling That Holds Two Fleets Apart
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra issues a masterful final insurance determination declaring the Kestrel a biohazard under joint quarantine—legally untouchable by either fleet. Beat: triumph that tastes like ash; the lie at its peak.

chapters.title: Quarantine Is a Cage
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Quarantine protects the Kestrel but condemns the crew to slow memory death without outside medical help. Sefa accuses Petra of saving the lie instead of the people. Beat: love's first real fracture.

chapters.title: What Justice Looks Like Out Here
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Haunted, Petra revisits his old testimony files and admits his lifelong pattern: hiding behind procedure instead of doing right. Beat: the moral pivot—he decides the truth must come out, somehow.

chapters.title: The Invitation Decoded
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Working through the night, Sefa completes the vector's message: it offers transformation to any civilization ready for it—not a weapon, a door. But doors can be forced. Beat: hope with a knife's edge.

chapters.title: Both Fleets Converge
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Quarantine collapses when a Concord captain declares it fraudulent; forty warships from both fleets burn toward the station. Petra's lie has hours left. Beat: dread at full pitch.

chapters.title: Halvorsen's Choice
chapters.summary: Halvorsen's POV. Ordered to seize the Kestrel by force, Halvorsen hesitates—he came for justice, not slaughter. He gives Petra one hour of silence. Beat: an enemy becoming an accomplice.

chapters.title: Evacuating the Unbecoming
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The crew evacuates the most-reversed members to medical ships under white flags. Okoro, half-gone, squeezes Sefa's hand and says thank you. Beat: grace amid catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Room
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra reaches the station's transmission array—the same room from Sefa's visions. He loads the full truth: the vector, the contact, the cover-up, his own lies. Beat: the climactic threshold, fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Truth at Light Speed
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He broadcasts everything to both fleets and the whole system, then surrenders his credentials. Warships stall mid-burn; the weapon everyone wanted is now common knowledge and therefore worthless as a monopoly. Beat: catharsis—the lie dies, the peace holds.

chapters.title: The Fleets Answer
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Concord and Meridian command react: fury, then grudging stand-down as public outrage erupts across both civilizations. Halvorsen testifies to corroborate. Beat: justice outside the law, messy and real.

chapters.title: Courtroom of Contested Orbits
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra faces a joint tribunal for fraud and obstruction. He pleads guilty to every count and asks only that the Kestrel's crew be treated, not studied. Beat: accountability embraced without flinching.

chapters.title: Sefa's Testimony
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa testifies about the vector's true nature and defends Petra's motive without excusing his methods. She plays the decoded invitation publicly. Beat: love expressed as truth-telling, the theme resolved.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra receives a suspended sentence and permanent exile from investigation work—effectively erasing the identity he hid behind. Beat: loss that is also liberation.

chapters.title: Younger Than Our Memories
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Treatment stabilizes the crew; some memories return, some don't. Sefa chooses not to recover her oldest memories, keeping the new life she's building. Beat: bittersweet acceptance of change.

chapters.title: The Door Still Open
chapters.summary: Shared POV. A joint civilian mission forms to answer the vector openly—as contact, not conquest. Sefa is asked to pilot; she says yes. Beat: hope institutionalized, the future chosen together.

chapters.title: Kestrel Rising
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra, identity-less and free, signs onto the mission as a simple cargo hand—the invisibility he once fled, now chosen. He and Sefa watch the vector's coordinates on the nav display. Beat: quiet joy, full-circle belonging.

chapters.title: Answering the Light
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs, final chapter. The Kestrel departs toward the signal with both fleets' banners flying as escort rather than threat. Sefa's last forward-memory arrives: this moment, exactly, and nothing beyond—because the future is finally unwritten. Beat: love against duty resolved into love as duty; the door opens.
